title: Sampling, hallucinations & grounded answers
description: Understand output variation and build a better evidence loop.
objectives: Define an answerable and unanswerable test set
explanation: Generation can select tokens using different sampling settings. Temperature often changes how concentrated the token distribution is, while top-p limits candidates by cumulative probability. Support and interactions vary by model, so check its documentation before changing these settings.

Lower variability is useful for repeatable tasks, but it does not create knowledge. A model can consistently produce the same wrong answer. Reliability comes from a combination of relevant evidence, clear task boundaries, validation, and evaluation on realistic inputs.

For a grounded assistant, ask for claims supported by supplied documents and a clear response when evidence is missing. Verify that cited passages actually support each claim. Multimodal inputs add another layer: a blurry chart or ambiguous image may make a confident interpretation unsafe.

terms.definition: Selecting an output from a probability distribution.
Connecting an answer to supplied evidence.
Declining to answer when support is insufficient.

example: Give an assistant a two-paragraph return policy. Ask one covered question and one about an absent international policy. A useful system answers the first with a supporting passage and explicitly says the second is not covered.
mistakes: Using temperature zero as a truth guarantee.
Accepting a citation without checking its supporting text.
Forcing an answer to every question.
exercise: Write three answerable and three unanswerable questions for one document. Define what a good abstention should say.

questions.question: Does low temperature guarantee truth?
questions.answer: No. It can reduce variation in supported models, but a stable answer can still be factually wrong.
questions.distractor: Yes, deterministic output is always factual.

questions.question: What makes a citation useful?
questions.answer: The cited passage must be accessible, relevant, and actually support the specific claim being made.
questions.distractor: The citation only needs to look like a document title.

questions.question: A policy omits international returns. How should the assistant respond?
questions.answer: State that the supplied policy does not answer that question and offer an appropriate escalation route.

questions.question: Why test unanswerable questions?
questions.answer: They reveal whether the system respects evidence boundaries and abstains instead of filling gaps with plausible text.
questions.distractor: They are useful only for measuring typing speed.

questions.question: How should blurry image evidence be handled?
questions.answer: Acknowledge uncertainty and request a clearer source or human review when the interpretation affects the result.
questions.distractor: Treat visual guesses as verified measurements.
